Job Description
Submarine Navigation Operators operate electronic equipment used for detection, tracking, recognition and identification of maritime vessels and aids to
navigation; operate and perform preventive maintenance on Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR) systems, Interior Communications (IC) circuits and
systems, fathometers, Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS), alarm systems, ship’s control stations, entertainment systems, Inertial
Navigation System (INS), Central Atmosphere Monitoring System (CAMS), Navigation Processor Unit (NPU), Remote Interface Controller (RIC), liquid
level detection and Tank Level Indication (TLI) circuits, flowmeters, pressure and temperature sensing circuits, valve position indicators, hovering systems,
depth control systems, fiber optic systems, Linux-based systems, and missile compensation systems; procure, inventory, and update electronic charts and
publications; prepare navigation voyage plans and maintain electronic navigation logs and records; stand navigation watches; advise and make reports to
the Officer of the Deck (OOD) on Navigation Rules and Regulations, navigation plans, and other navigation matters; and report to/work under direct
supervision of the Submarine Navigation Technician and Submarine Navigation Manager.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
